claims.title: Sensor readings may be intercepted between field nodes and the internet-facing gateway
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings` resolves to no effective transport protection, an observer on the field-network-to-ingest-edge path can intercept the PII-tagged sensor readings and device identifiers sent to `process:device-gateway`. The flow crosses from customer-controlled field sites to the ingest edge, so a compromised local network or intermediary can collect readings without authenticating to the gateway. Second-order, accumulated device identifiers and readings can be correlated with the customer assignments that `process:device-gateway` resolves through `store:device-registry`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings` crosses a trust boundary but its `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and exposes readings associated with device identifiers from customer sites.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for node MQTT sessions
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:sensor-node>process:device-gateway>publish-readings` and record the verified `encryption_in_transit` setting; use mutual TLS where device identity can support it.

mitigations.summary: Minimize identifying metadata in readings
mitigations.detail: Use opaque device references where possible so captured telemetry does not directly expose stable customer-device identifiers.

claims.title: Fleet key material may be intercepted on the gateway registry lookup
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device` resolves to no effective protection, an attacker able to observe the ingest-edge service path can intercept device identifiers, customer assignments, and the key material sent to `store:device-registry`. The registry contains credentials, and the disclosed fleet pre-shared key can then be used to authenticate nodes to `process:device-gateway`; that later use is spoofing, while this draft concerns the credential disclosure.

quotes.text: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the transport setting is unknown and an attacker must first obtain an observation position on the internal gateway-to-registry path. Impact is high because `store:device-registry` is confidential and tagged `credentials`, and its fleet key can enable later authentication to the internet-facing gateway.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the registry connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS, preferably mTLS, on `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device` and verify the Firestore endpoint identity.

mitigations.summary: Stop sending reusable fleet key material on lookups
mitigations.detail: Use a narrowly scoped verifier or derived credential check so the gateway does not transmit reusable pre-shared key material to the registry.

claims.title: Customer occupancy data may be intercepted while the normalizer loads the telemetry lake
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:telemetry-lake>load-readings` resolves to no effective protection, an observer on the analytics-core path can intercept site addresses, occupancy patterns, and readings while `process:telemetry-normalizer` writes them to `store:telemetry-lake`. This is conditional on the unverified transport setting; it is not an assertion that BigQuery transport is cleartext. Second-order, the captured data enables physical and behavioural profiling of customer premises without needing dashboard access.

quotes.text: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the unverified link is internal and requires an attacker to obtain an analytics-network observation position. Impact is high because `store:telemetry-lake` is confidential and holds PII including customer site addresses and occupancy patterns.

mitigations.summary: Verify encrypted transport to BigQuery
mitigations.detail: Require and document TLS 1.2+ on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:telemetry-lake>load-readings`, including certificate validation by `process:telemetry-normalizer`.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive fields on the ingestion path
mitigations.detail: Tokenize or separate site-address fields before the normalizer writes readings where the analytics workflow does not need the raw address.

claims.title: Dashboard queries may expose customer telemetry across the corporate-to-analytics boundary
claims.description: If `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:fleet-operator>store:telemetry-lake>query-dashboards` resolves to no effective protection, an attacker able to observe the corporate-network-to-analytics-core path can intercept the aggregated and raw customer readings returned from `store:telemetry-lake` to `entity:fleet-operator`. The flow crosses a derived trust boundary and carries PII and business-critical data. Second-order, raw occupancy patterns and site addresses allow the observer to infer when customer premises are occupied, without obtaining the operator's company SSO session.

quotes.text: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the query crosses from the corporate network into the analytics core while `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is high because the confidential lake contains PII, site addresses, and occupancy patterns, and the flow returns both aggregated and raw readings.

mitigations.summary: Enforce TLS for dashboard data retrieval
mitigations.detail: Verify TLS and endpoint identity on `flow:entity:fleet-operator>store:telemetry-lake>query-dashboards`; do not rely on corporate-network placement as a confidentiality control.

mitigations.summary: Return minimized dashboard data
mitigations.detail: Restrict dashboard responses to the aggregate and fields required for each operator view, rather than routinely returning raw customer readings.

claims.title: Accepted telemetry may be intercepted on the gateway-to-Pub/Sub hop
claims.description: If the unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit` state on `flow:process:device-gateway>store:pub-sub>forward-readings` resolve to an unprotected transport, an observer on that service path can intercept the PII-tagged normalized sensor readings submitted by `process:device-gateway` to `store:pub-sub`. This is conditional on both unverified transport facts. Second-order, the captured stream can be correlated with later telemetry-lake records and used to profile customer sites outside the authorized analytics path.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the hop is internal and both its protocol and transport protection are unverified. Impact is medium because the Pub/Sub path carries PII-tagged normalized sensor readings that can be correlated with customer telemetry.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated encrypted Pub/Sub transport
mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:process:device-gateway>store:pub-sub>forward-readings` to use a verified TLS-protected protocol and record the resulting protocol and `encryption_in_transit` attributes.

mitigations.summary: Limit telemetry retained in message payloads
mitigations.detail: Use opaque references or tokenize direct identifiers in Pub/Sub messages where the consumer can resolve them under its own authorization.

claims.title: Telemetry may be intercepted as the normalizer consumes Pub/Sub messages
claims.description: If the unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit` state on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings` resolve to an unprotected transport, an observer on the analytics-core-to-ingest-edge path can intercept PII-tagged normalized readings as `process:telemetry-normalizer` consumes them from `store:pub-sub`. This flow crosses a trust boundary, and the disclosure lets the observer collect the same stream that is subsequently loaded into `store:telemetry-lake`.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses between analytics core and ingest edge while both protocol and transport encryption are unverified. Impact is medium because the messages are tagged PII and expose the customer telemetry stream before it reaches the lake.

mitigations.summary: Protect the Pub/Sub consumer connection in transit
mitigations.detail: Require verified TLS for `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings` and validate the broker identity from `process:telemetry-normalizer`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain subscriber payload visibility
mitigations.detail: Use separate subscriptions and minimized message schemas so each consumer receives only fields it requires.

claims.title: A storage copy of the device registry may reveal fleet credentials
claims.description: `store:device-registry` is confidential, holds credentials, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to storage without effective encryption, an attacker who obtains a backup, snapshot, exported copy, or decommissioned storage artifact can read the fleet pre-shared key checks and customer assignments without authenticating through `process:device-gateway`. Second-order, a recovered fleet key can be presented to the gateway as a node credential; that subsequent identity abuse is outside this disclosure draft.

quotes.text: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value: obtaining an operational copy is a prerequisite, but such a copy bypasses application authentication if encryption is absent. Impact is high because `store:device-registry` is confidential and tagged `credentials`, and the disclosed fleet key enables later gateway authentication.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption at rest for registry copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture of `store:device-registry` and require managed-key encryption for the primary store, backups, exports, snapshots, and replicas.

mitigations.summary: Replace the shared fleet pre-shared key
mitigations.detail: Move to per-device, rotatable credentials so one storage-copy disclosure does not expose an entire fleet identity.

claims.title: A telemetry-lake storage copy may disclose customer addresses and occupancy patterns
claims.description: `store:telemetry-lake` is confidential, holds PII and business-critical data, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to no effective encryption at rest, an attacker holding a backup, snapshot, export, or decommissioned media copy can read site addresses, occupancy patterns, and readings directly, bypassing `entity:fleet-operator`'s company SSO path. Second-order, the copied corpus supports persistent profiling of customer premises even after live access is removed.

quotes.text: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the lake's encryption-at-rest state is unverified and a storage copy must be obtained. Impact is high because `store:telemetry-lake` is confidential and contains PII, customer site addresses, and occupancy patterns; copied personal data cannot be recalled.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the lake and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:telemetry-lake` encryption at rest and enforce managed-key encryption for BigQuery exports, backups, snapshots, replicas, and any lower-environment copies.

mitigations.summary: Restrict export and key-use permissions
mitigations.detail: Separate data-read, export, and key-decrypt privileges so an account able to query the lake cannot automatically obtain a portable readable copy.

claims.title: A retained Pub/Sub copy may disclose telemetry if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:pub-sub` is tagged PII and its `data_classification` and `encryption_at_rest` are both unknown. If retained Pub/Sub messages are stored without effective encryption at rest, an attacker obtaining a retained-message export, backup, or storage-layer copy can read normalized sensor readings without authenticating as `process:telemetry-normalizer`. This is conditional on the unresolved classification and encryption posture; it does not assert that Pub/Sub storage is unencrypted. Second-order, the messages can be correlated with telemetry-lake data to build customer activity profiles.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because both the retained-data classification and encryption-at-rest posture of `store:pub-sub` are unverified, while a copied retained payload bypasses live subscriber controls. Impact is medium because the store is tagged PII and carries normalized sensor readings, although the model does not establish the retention scope or classification.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce Pub/Sub retention encryption
mitigations.detail: Record the `data_classification` and `encryption_at_rest` posture for `store:pub-sub`, and require encryption for retained messages, exports, and operational copies.

mitigations.summary: Limit message retention and export access
mitigations.detail: Set the shortest feasible retention period and restrict export or subscription-administration rights to separate narrowly scoped principals.

claims.title: Code in the internet-facing gateway can recover fleet credentials from the registry
claims.description: `process:device-gateway` is internet-facing and reads `store:device-registry` through `flow:process:device-gateway>store:device-registry>look-up-device`; the registry holds confidential credential material used to check fleet keys. An attacker who achieves code execution in the gateway or controls its runtime can use the gateway's existing read path to recover fleet key material and customer assignments. The read-path authentication is unknown, so the scope of the gateway's registry grant is unverified. Second-order, recovered fleet keys can be used to authenticate to the gateway as nodes, enabling subsequent spoofing attempts.

quotes.text: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE and expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere.
The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:device-gateway` is expressly internet-facing, though the attacker must first obtain execution in that component and the registry-flow authentication is unknown. Impact is high because the confidential `store:device-registry` holds credentials and a fleet key can enable later authentication as a node.

mitigations.summary: Constrain gateway access to credential material
mitigations.detail: Replace broad registry reads with a narrowly scoped verification operation that returns only an allow or deny result and never returns reusable key material.

mitigations.summary: Use workload identity and least-privilege registry access
mitigations.detail: Set a dedicated `process:device-gateway` identity with only the registry fields and operations required, and log anomalous bulk or credential-field reads.

mitigations.summary: Use per-device rotatable credentials
mitigations.detail: Replace fleet-shared pre-shared keys with individual short-lived or rotatable device credentials so recovery from one gateway runtime has limited reach.

claims.title: Code in the telemetry normalizer can read retained PII from Pub/Sub
claims.description: `process:telemetry-normalizer` reads PII-tagged normalized readings from `store:pub-sub` through `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:pub-sub>pick-up-readings`. An attacker who runs code in the normalizer can consume that stream using the component's existing access, rather than needing a storage copy or an operator session. The consumer-flow authentication is unknown, so the identity and scope that permit this read are unverified. Second-order, the attacker can correlate the stream with the data later written to `store:telemetry-lake` to infer customer site activity.

quotes.text: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because an attacker must first obtain execution in the internal `process:telemetry-normalizer`, although the authentication for its Pub/Sub read path is unknown. Impact is medium because `store:pub-sub` is tagged PII and the component can read normalized telemetry that can be correlated with customer activity.

mitigations.summary: Use a narrowly scoped subscriber identity
mitigations.detail: Set a dedicated authenticated identity for `process:telemetry-normalizer` with access only to its required subscription and record the flow's authentication method.

mitigations.summary: Minimize and isolate telemetry subscriptions
mitigations.detail: Separate subscriptions by purpose and minimize PII in messages so compromise of one consumer does not reveal the full retained telemetry stream.
